text.text_excerpt: We stayed here for 5 nights and it was really good for the price. Like everyone else is saying, it sure as heck aint fancy, and don't bet on the continental breakfast too hard, since it consists of only waffles, apples, yogurt and bread. Yikes! But it was clean, comfortable, quiet, and had good housekeeping! (There is a pool but it was wayyy too cold to swim) My only complaint is that the wifi was spotty and slow, and the cable sucks, haha, but who comes to NOLA to watch cable and surf the internet?! The people at the front desk were lovely, friendly, helpful, and totally hilarious. We really enjoyed staying here, and we would come back. As everyone else is saying, the area seems to be a ...

Good value, comfortable and clean, friendly staff. Not a place for you if you want an upscale neighborhood and lodging, but it's fine if you just want a clean, basic place to stay. Free parking, free breakfast, free wi fi. They also have a small fitness room and a pool. Reception desk employee was very friendly at check-in. Our maid, Ms. Cathy, left us a cute note thanking us for being "clean people". Food: Breakfast wasn't anything fancy (frosted flakes, raisin bran, toast with jam or butter, waffles and syrup or butter, juice, coffee, pastries, and some yogurt), but was ok for getting something in your stomach. Room: Bed was firm but not hard. Pillows were ok. Room was clean. Microwave ...

Decent place out in the neighborhoods, right next to I10; not fancy, clean and comfortable. People call the neighborhood sketchy but staff pays a lot of attention to security. We ate at "Louisiana Pride" about a mile further into the neighborhood, had a great meal (5 lbs boiled crawfish) and talked to some great people that live there. Super 8 is about a 15 minute drive to catch a streetcar on either Canal line during commute times. Room had a bed, shower, microwave, refer, table and chairs. Considering that we spent our days streetcaring, eating, kayaking and drinking, what more do you need?
